newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian dlr ends back where it started.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian dlr ends back where it started.

text.p: The Australian dollar ended Monday back where it started it, having been held to a 10 point range on a day lacking leads both locally and internationally, traders said.

At 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT) the Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7906/11, from an early US$0.7905/10 and a local close to last week of US$0.7890/95. On the day, the unit traded a US$0.7899-7908 range.
The key local event for the week is the Wednesday release of the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) bulletin, which will contain the RBA's quarterly assessment of the economy and its prospects.
With the only other major data of the week being Friday's imports data, traders said there was little impetus for the market at the start of the week.

Ahead of the Colombus Day holiday today, the U.S. dollar held fairly steady in quiet Tokyo trading, keeping the Australian dollar reasonably steady also. Officially the U.S. market is open today, but trade is expected to be minimal.

The local dollar finished at 88.30/40 yen, slightly up on its opening 88.22/32 and above its Friday close of 87.85/95. In trade weighted terms, the unit has remained unchanged at 58.4 since Friday afternoon.

Across the Tasman, the New Zealand dollar rallied half a U.S. cent despite the fact that no coalition government had emerged from weekend elections as declining support for the far left Alliance party saw shorts covering their positions today.
For the Australian dollar, the month-long US$0.7855/7965 range is not seen under threat in the early part of the week.

Support is seen at US$0.7870, the level that held after the dollar dipped to on last Thursday's weaker than expected labour force data. The resilience of that support surprised many in the market, and led to the conclusion that a 50 basis point near term easing had been factored into the market.
The holding of that level also indicated that the market may be a touch short of the Australian dollar and looking to buy on the dips, traders said.
On the topside, US$0.7925 is seen as initial key resistance, with the mixed performance of commodities and the rate cut undercutting the Australian dollar's yield differential.

As well there was some talk in the bill market that another rate cut will be delivered in early 1997. March bill futures closed Monday at 93.66, an implied yield 66 basis points under the 7.0 percent official cash rate.

With the U.S. dollar sidelined in Tokyo, attention was on the European currencies following the weekend announcement that the Finnish markka would join the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM). However, it was one of the four European Union currencies outside the ERM that took centre stage.
Sterling rose to its highest level since early 1993 against the yen in Tokyo trading, after surging on Friday in New York on a well received ruling Conservative Party conference.
Traders said the other European currency to watch was the Italian lire, which has been the subject of speculation that it would soon join the ERM. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
